content.text: Fedora's WSDL does not declare faults.  As a consequence, when going against the SOAP interfaces, this causes a generic fault to be thrown when errors occur.

Better would be to use WSDL faults, which map to SOAP faults, which can include error codes, which clients can interpret.   There are many references online that detail how to do this.  For starters, google(wsdl faults best practice)
Not enough time to address this for 3.2; pushed to a future release.
This is important to us as a larger institution because the REST API can't support this kind of error flow-back reporting, which is extremely helpful for extensive workflows,
Jiri Kremser will be addressing this as part of his Google Summer of Code project:

Fedora's WSDL does not declare faults. As a consequence, when going against the SOAP interfaces, this causes a generic fault to be thrown when errors occur.

Better would be to use WSDL faults, which map to SOAP faults, which can include error codes, which clients can interpret. There are many references online that detail how to do this. For starters, google(wsdl faults best practice)
